The partition key determines how items are distributed across physical partitions and groups items with the same key value into a logical partition so related data stays co‑located — this makes queries within that logical partition efficient and scopes transactions to a single logical partition [1]. Choosing a good partition key (high cardinality) also helps spread storage and request volume evenly to avoid hot partitions [2].

Use Azure Service Bus for the messaging layer and run the worker in Azure Container Apps with a KEDA scale rule on the Service Bus queue.

- Service Bus is a fully managed enterprise message broker with queues suitable for competing-consumers/work-distribution scenarios like background workers [3][1].  
- The canonical pattern is a KEDA scale rule on Service Bus queue depth so the worker scales out as the queue deepens and back to zero when it drains [2].  
- Azure Container Apps uses KEDA-based autoscaling, supports scale rules driven by Service Bus queue length, and can scale to zero—no compute charges accrue while an app is at zero replicas [8][2].

The reliability pillar says to deploy redundant instances across fault domains so no single failure takes the workload down [2]. Availability zones are fault-isolated, physically separate data centers (independent power, cooling, networking), and zone‑reduant deployments spread replicas across zones so loss of a single zone does not take the application/workload down [2][1]. Design for failure is the guiding principle behind this approach [3].
